questions.enonce_markdown:
Define each of the following terms and give an example in each case:

(i) Cell

(ii) Tissue

(iii) Organ. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **cell** is the **basic structural and functional unit of living organisms**; it is the smallest unit that can carry out all the characteristics of life. *Example:* a red blood cell (or a nerve cell, a muscle cell).

(ii) A **tissue** is a **group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function**. *Example:* muscle tissue (or epithelial tissue, blood, nervous tissue).

(iii) An **organ** is a **structure made of two or more different tissues that work together to perform a particular function**. *Example:* the heart (or the stomach, the lung, the skin, the kidney).

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of a typical animal cell as seen under the electron microscope. *(8 marks)*
In tabular form, distinguish between a typical animal cell and a typical bacterial cell. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Typical animal cell | Typical bacterial cell |
|---|---|
| Eukaryotic: has a true nucleus bounded by a nuclear envelope | Prokaryotic: no true nucleus; the genetic material (a single circular DNA molecule) lies free in the cytoplasm in a nucleoid region |
| Large (about 10 - 100 $\mu$m) | Small (about 1 - 5 $\mu$m) |
| No cell wall; only a cell membrane | Has a cell wall made of peptidoglycan (murein) outside the cell membrane |
| Has membrane-bound organelles (mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes) | No membrane-bound organelles |
| Ribosomes are large (80S) | Ribosomes are smaller (70S) |
| Several linear chromosomes made of DNA and protein (histones) | One circular chromosome (and often small plasmids), not associated with histone proteins |
| Divides by mitosis (or meiosis) | Divides by binary fission |
| No capsule or bacterial flagella (some cells have cilia) | May have a capsule, flagella or pili |
